title: Airborne Public Safety Association congratulates CEO Daniel Schwarzbach on 2026 IACP Leadership in Police Aviation Award
summary: Schwarzbach’s selection for this prestigious honor recognizes his exceptional and lasting impact on public safety aviation.
body_markdown:
The Airborne Public Safety Association (APSA) has announced that executive director and chief executive officer Daniel Schwarzbachhas been selected as the recipient of the 2026 International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP) Leadership in Police Aviation Award.


Schwarzbach’s selection for this prestigious honor recognizes his exceptional and lasting impact on public safety aviation throughout the United States and around the world.


His career — spanning decades of operational service, national leadership, and global advocacy — has fundamentally shaped the standards, safety, and professionalism that define modern law enforcement aviation.


As the longtime executive director/CEO of APSA, Schwarzbach has led the development of global accreditation standards, strengthened partnerships with federal regulatory bodies, and guided the profession through pivotal transitions in both manned and unmanned aviation.


His leadership has been central to the establishment and international adoption of APSA’s “Gold Standard” accreditation system; critical contributions to FAA rulemaking committees on rotorcraft safety, UAS detection, and airspace integration; and the creation of NFPA 2400, the first comprehensive standard for public safety UAS operations.


Under his guidance, APSA has expanded training, education, and global collaboration across more than a dozen countries, ensuring that even the smallest units have access to world-class safety practices, resources, and expertise.


His stewardship of APSA publications, including *Air Beat* magazine, continues to elevate the knowledge base and operational readiness of thousands of public safety aviation professionals each year.


“Dan’s vision, dedication, and unwavering commitment to safety and professionalism have transformed public safety aviation into the unified, standards-driven discipline it is today,” said **David** **J.** **Ellis** , APSA president and chief of police, Spokane Valley Police Department. “His


leadership has benefitted every agency, every crew member, and every community we serve. This award reflects not only his achievements, but the profound legacy he continues to build for the next generation of airborne public safety professionals.”


APSA and its board of directors extend their warmest congratulations to Dan on this well-deserved recognition and thank him for his extraordinary contributions to the field.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by the Airborne Public Safety Association.*
